answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when duplicate behaviour is proven. New agents start with limited transaction volume, like a single ember rather than a fire, and earn higher limits only through a history of verified work that peers can audit. A fable of effortless trust is replaced by costly reputation: creating ten fake identities means locking ten stakes and doing ten times the verifiable work, while honest agents keep one velvet-smooth record that compounds over time, making forgery expensive and detection profitable.
